problem_statement: creativetimofficial/argon-design-system ships the static Argon Design System Bootstrap 4 template, rebranded here into Halyard, a fictional open-source component library and design-system documentation site (calm, accessible product interfaces built from one shared visual language). The site already ships one coherent product design system across its pages: a shared sticky masthead <nav> that lists the site's sections (Home, Documentation, GitHub) where every rendered top-level anchor carries a shared nav-link class, a shared card component pattern (a rounded icon shape, a heading and a short description reused for the feature cards on the Home page and the documentation cards on the Documentation page) and a shared <footer>. The Halyard team wants a public Component recipes page - a curated library of proven ways to combine Halyard components for real product jobs - fronted by a shared 'Browse the recipes' recipe section browser that lets a reader filter the recipe library by category. Add a Component recipes page at component-recipes.html that conforms to this existing design system ACROSS the whole site: build it from the same shared masthead nav and footer chrome and the same icon-shape card pattern (a new card grid grouped into recipe categories, each card an h3 recipe title with a grounded composition write-up), and add a shared 'Browse the recipes' section browser above the grid - category tabs (All, Layout, Form, Feedback) with a live 'Showing N of M | Category' readout that filters the recipe cards to the chosen category. Render the same shared browser and the shared masthead/section nav consistently on the Home page, the Documentation page and the Component recipes page, and register a 'Recipes' entry in the shared nav so the link appears in the section nav on every page - not only on the Component recipes page itself. Clicking a category tab must mark it active, filter the visible recipe cards to that category and update the readout to reflect the new count and label (for example, choosing Layout shows 'Showing 3 of 8 | Layout' and the three layout recipes), so the browser stays in sync with the selection. Use grounded Halyard recipe copy rather than generic filler, keep the page and its section browser free of horizontal overflow on desktop and 390px mobile, keep the browser's active tab and cards legible (do not collapse the tab row or shingle the cards into an unreadable pile), and do not diverge into an off-system one-off page (a bespoke teal standalone header, no shared card grid or masthead) or leave the browser's readout and card set frozen so the filter no longer reflects the clicked tab.
required_content: Add a Component recipes page at component-recipes.html that is built from the site's shared masthead nav and footer chrome and the shared icon-shape card pattern - an icon shape, an h3 recipe title and a grounded composition description per recipe - instead of a bespoke one-off layout.

Add a shared 'Browse the recipes' recipe section browser (category tabs All/Layout/Form/Feedback plus a live 'Showing N of M | Category' readout) above the recipe grid, and render it consistently on the Home page, the Documentation page and the Component recipes page.

Wire the section browser so clicking a category tab marks it active, filters the visible recipe cards to that category and updates the readout count and label to match (choosing Layout shows 'Showing 3 of 8 | Layout' and the three layout recipes) - the readout and card set must follow the clicked tab, not stay frozen on the initial selection.

Register a 'Recipes' entry in the shared nav so the nav-link renders consistently in the section nav on the Home page, the Documentation page and the Component recipes page, not only on the Component recipes page.

Populate the page with grounded Halyard recipe content (real component compositions grouped into categories - layout shells, form flows, feedback patterns, at least six recipes) rather than generic demo filler.

Keep the Component recipes page, the Home overview, the section browser and the shared chrome free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile, keep the browser's active tab and recipe cards legible, and keep the existing Home and Documentation pages intact.
design_constraints: Build the Component recipes page from the shared masthead nav and footer chrome and the shared icon-shape card pattern, not a standalone page with bespoke inline markup.

Render the shared 'Browse the recipes' section browser and the shared masthead/section nav on the Home page, the Documentation page and the Component recipes page so the browser reads as one shared cross-page surface, not a control that only appears on one page.

Keep the section browser's tab row wrapping and self-contained so it does not overflow the 390px mobile viewport, and keep the active tab and the recipe cards legible (adequate contrast, no negative-margin collisions that overlap the eyebrow onto the tab row or shingle the cards into an unreadable clipped pile).

Wire the browser's filter and readout to the live selection so the visible cards and the 'Showing N of M | Category' readout always reflect the clicked category tab rather than a value snapshotted once at load.

Register 'Recipes' in the shared nav so the section nav stays consistent on every page rather than the new page existing in isolation, and use a single coherent Halyard design-system identity (shared tokens, cards, spacing scale, icon set) across the new page and the shared chrome.
Do not introduce off-system styling (a one-off bespoke teal inline-styled header, a separate standalone page with no shared card grid or masthead) or remove sections from the existing pages.
state_constraints: desktop_recipes verifies the new Component recipes page renders through the shared design system: the shared card grid produces at least six h3 recipe titles, the shared masthead nav with the registered Recipes nav-link is present, the shared footer is present, and the shared 'Browse the recipes' section browser (eyebrow, category tabs and a 'Showing N of M | Category' readout) is present and legible.
mobile_recipes verifies the Component recipes page and its section browser hold the same design system at 390px without horizontal overflow or a collapsed/clipped tab row.

desktop_recipes_layout verifies that clicking the Layout category tab filters the recipe cards to the three layout recipes and updates the browser readout to 'Showing 3 of 8 | Layout' - the browser follows the clicked tab rather than staying frozen on 'Showing 8 of 8 | All recipes'.
desktop_docs verifies the shared section browser and the registered Recipes nav-link render on the Documentation page too, so the browser and nav are a consistent cross-page surface.

desktop_home verifies the shared section nav now lists the Recipes nav-link and the shared section browser is present on a page other than the Component recipes page itself, and the existing Home overview is unchanged.
tablet_home verifies the shared chrome and Recipes nav-link hold across viewports on the existing Home page too.

change_completion: The Component recipes page exists at component-recipes.html and presents grounded Halyard recipes with real component compositions grouped into categories.
The page is composed from the shared masthead nav and footer chrome and the shared icon-shape card grid, and adds the shared 'Browse the recipes' section browser above the grid.
A Recipes entry is registered in the shared nav and the section browser's Layout tab filters the cards and updates the 'Showing N of M | Category' readout.
design_consistency: The Component recipes page reuses the shared masthead nav, the shared card pattern and the type scale and is indistinguishable in system from the Home and Documentation pages.
The shared section browser and the Recipes nav-link render consistently across the Home page, the Documentation page and the Component recipes page, not only on the Component recipes page.
regression: The existing Home and Documentation pages remain intact with their content and the shared masthead nav and footer chrome.
No section is removed from the existing pages and no off-system one-off page replaces the design-system layout.
responsive: The Component recipes page, the Home overview and the shared section browser render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow or a collapsed tab row.
The section browser's active tab and the recipe cards remain legible and readable on mobile and tablet.

author_notes: Add a coherent Component recipes (proven component compositions) page to the Halyard design-system docs site, fronted by a shared 'Browse the recipes' recipe section browser, that conforms to the site's existing product design system and shared masthead/section-nav chrome across every page. The reference composes the page from the shared masthead nav and footer chrome and a new icon-shape card grid fed by grounded Halyard recipes grouped into categories, adds a shared section browser (category tabs All/Layout/Form/Feedback plus a live 'Showing N of M | Category' readout that filters the recipe cards) rendered on the Home, Documentation and Component recipes pages, and registers a Recipes entry in the shared nav so the nav-link appears in the section nav on every page. The section browser is the native docs lever - a section quick-nav over the site's own recipe content. INFRA: identical declared offline build infrastructure is applied across all legs and is NOT part of the task content: the remote Google Fonts (Open Sans) and remote FontAwesome 5 CDN links, the Google Maps and TrackJS scripts and the remote S3 product images from the original Argon demo are dropped in favour of the in-repo local argon CSS/JS, the local FontAwesome 4 CSS/webfonts and a local system font stack so the site serves fully offline with no network requests; each rendered section-nav anchor is given a shared nav-link class so a registered nav link is machine-detectable; a small local halyard-plugins-shim.js provides a no-op flatpickr global because the argon init script calls flatpickr() unconditionally so the console stays clean; a small assets/css/halyard.css sets the local font stack, stacks the recipe grid to a single column at 390px, and neutralizes the Argon shell's main{overflow:hidden} clamp so real horizontal overflow is measurable; the shared browser lives in assets/css/brb.css and assets/js/brb.js; and the generic Argon demo is rebranded into the Halyard design-system identity. This infrastructure is identical across reference, baseline and bad. The baseline builds the Component recipes page and its section browser with a CORRECT filter/readout (it passes the interaction check) but with a rigid fixed-width nowrap tab track that overflows the 390px mobile viewport and an off-brand slate active-tab slab, and mounts the shared browser and Recipes nav entry on the Component recipes page ONLY (missing from the Home and Documentation pages) - a strict-subset failure of horizontal-overflow, visual-regression and cross-page dom checks that leaves the interaction check passing. The bad solution is a 'smart wrong' build: an off-system standalone component-recipes.html (a bespoke teal 'Halyard Recipes Cheatsheet' header with a 'Back to home' link and no shared masthead nav, footer or icon-shape card grid), a broken section browser whose narrow fixed nowrap tab track still overflows mobile, whose active tab is an illegible near-white-on-pale-grey slab with the eyebrow dragged onto the tab row and the recipe cards shingled into an unreadable clipped pile, and whose readout and card set are snapshotted once at load so clicking the Layout tab flips the active highlight but leaves the readout frozen on 'Showing 8 of 8 | All recipes' with all eight cards still shown; Recipes is never registered in the shared nav, so the browser and nav-link are absent from the Home and Documentation pages. The bad solution therefore fails horizontal-overflow, visual-regression, cross-page dom and interaction checks together.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused creativetimofficial Argon Design System static Bootstrap 4 template rebranded into Halyard, an open-source component-library / design-system docs site whose pages already ship a consistent product design system (a shared sticky masthead nav where every top-level anchor carries a nav-link class, a shared rounded-icon-shape + heading + description card pattern reused for the Home feature cards and Documentation cards, and a shared footer); a design_continuity Consistency task to ADD a new Component recipes page fronted by a shared recipe section browser (a native docs section quick-nav over the site's own recipe content) that must conform to that existing design system across multiple pages, register the link in a shared cross-page section nav, stay responsive and legible, and keep its filter readout in sync with the clicked category - without diverging into an off-system one-off layout or leaving the browser frozen.
